// SYNTH_CLOCKGATE_MIN_WIDTH: was 2, which gated every >=2-bit register and inserted 84 ICGs. Each dlclkp_2 in the clock path costs ~0.34 ns and forces CTS to build a 2-level subtree under it: on the o_m_axi_arlen[6] failing path the ICG _19713_ plus clkbuf_0__09612_/clkbuf_1_0__f__09612_ account for 0.79 ns of the 1.76 ns insertion delay. Output ports have no clock network on the capture side, so that 0.79 ns comes straight off setup margin -- 3.3x the -0.237 ns violation. 8 leaves u_dma.len_r[6:0] ungated. Costs some switching power (2.81 mW total today).
// CTS_BALANCE_LEVELS / CTS_OBSTRUCTION_: removed. OpenROAD logs '-balance_levels is obsolete' (CTS-0128) and '-obstruction_aware is obsolete' (CTS-0132) -- both were silently ignored. Obstruction awareness is unconditional in current TritonCTS.
// CTS_DELAY_BUFFER_DERATE_PCT: next experiment, change alone. Today CTS builds a 25-deep chain of clkbuf_16 delay buffers at the root; network latency is 1.723 ns min / 2.760 ns max (1.04 ns spread) on a 10 ns period. Derate scales how many balancing buffers get inserted (0 = none, 100 = full). Try 0 and 100 and compare: lower insertion delay helps every AXI output path 1:1, but less balancing costs skew and hold currently only has +0.158 ns WS.
// *_RESIZER_SETUP_SLACK_MARGIN: raised from 0.10. Stage 45 (post-GRT resizer) signed off at TNS 0.000 / ss WS 0.173, then stage 57 (post-DRT, real parasitics) came back at -0.237 -- the resizer stopped optimizing the moment it hit its 0.10 margin against GRT's estimated RC and had nothing left to absorb the routing delta. 0.30 at GRT gives it headroom to cover that gap.
